claims.text: Robert Jamison was a US Air Force 1st Lieutenant commanding an ICBM Combat Targeting Team at Malmstrom AFB, Montana, from January 1965 to October 1967, then a missile targeting instructor at Chanute AFB, Illinois, and separated from active duty as a Captain in July 1972. He executed an affidavit and appeared at the UFO-Nukes Connection press conference at the National Press Club on 27 September 2010.

label: Capt. Robert Jamison
narrative: Robert Jamison matters far more to the structure of the Malmstrom case than his profile suggests, and the reason is a date. He commanded an ICBM combat targeting team at Malmstrom from January 1965 to October 1967, and he describes being called out to retarget missiles after a second flight went off alert in March 1967, separately from the Echo Flight event of the sixteenth. It is his recollection that Robert Hastings gives as the basis for placing the Oscar Flight incident on 24 March 1967, eight days after Echo Flight. That separation is load-bearing for the whole cluster: for years the Oscar Flight account was told as part of the same 16 March event, which let Echo Flight's Tier 1 documentation be read as corroborating Salas. Once the two are separated, Echo Flight's paper no longer touches Oscar Flight and the Oscar Flight claim stands or falls on testimony alone. The board should hold that plainly: the fact that rescues the Oscar Flight account from the unit history's silence was supplied by a witness the same interviewer found, and no pre-contact statement by Jamison has been identified. He executed an affidavit and spoke on the record at the National Press Club on 27 September 2010, which is the dated artefact that fixes when the claim was made.
